assertion: Visibility was limited by darkness, although the roadway was illuminated
The vehicle was turning right when it came into contact with a parked vehicle
The claimant did not initially realize how significant the contact was
The claimant stopped briefly, looked at the vehicles, and then left because they were concerned about being stranded late at night
The claimant did not see anyone inside the parked vehicle
The claimant did not believe anyone was injured
The claimant was driving the Mercedes-Benz G-Class southbound and making a right turn at approximately 9:40 PM.
The claimant recalls that it had been raining earlier and that the pavement was wet.
The claimant was driving around 25 to 30 mph before beginning the turn.
The turn was normal until the vehicle suddenly slid.
The claimant tried to correct the vehicle, but the front of the Mercedes contacted a parked SUV.
The claimant did not see anyone inside the parked SUV and did not believe anyone was injured.
The claimant stopped after the collision, looked at the vehicles, and then left because they were concerned about being stranded late at night.
The claimant intended to report the incident.
The claimant does not recall the exact distance traveled, whether traction control activated, whether another vehicle was nearby, whether there was a witness, or the exact impact location.
